Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

voluntary adjective

also voluntarily, of one’s own free will, volunteer, volunteers, unpaid (of work), willing, volunteer (soldier), volunteer to do something

classical

Cic. Off. 1.28: sī est voluntārium (Lewis & Short)
Caes. B.C. 3.91, of soldiers: volunteers (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 188: volunteer, voluntārius (-a)
Traupman 402

voluntārius, voluntāria, voluntārium

Declension on Wiktionary

voluntary, done of one’s own will

Of people, willing, serving of their own accord; as a noun, voluntāriī m. pl. are volunteers (Caes., Liv.). Of things, done or chosen freely: discessus voluntārius, a departure of one’s own choosing (Cic. Att. 9.13.4).

Other words

  • meā (tuā, suā) sponte — voluntarily, of my (your, his) own accord

    phrase: ablative, in good prose always with the possessive · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 9.14.2: tuō jūdiciō et tuā sponte facere (Lewis & Short); Ter. Ad. 75 · Wiktionary

    The everyday way to say that someone did a thing without being made to.

  • grātuītus, grātuīta, grātuītum — unpaid, done for nothing

    also used · classical · Cic. Leg. 1.48: līberālitās grātuītane est an mercēnāria? (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    For voluntary work in the sense of unpaid: done without pay or reward.

Examples

  • Hoc patrium est, potius cōnsuēfacere fīlium suā sponte rēctē facere quam aliēnō metū.

    That is a father’s way: to get his son used to doing right of his own accord, rather than from fear of someone else.Ter. Ad. 74–75

  • movērī vetuisse puerum dōnec suā sponte experrēctus esset

    she forbade anyone to move the boy until he had woken up of his own accordLiv. 1.39.2

  • sponte nōmen dare

    to volunteer (for military service)Traupman 402

  • aliquid ultrō facere

    to volunteer to do somethingTraupman 402

  • mīles voluntārius

    a volunteer soldierTraupman 402

See also own, free.
